findings.body: A no-budget response returned after the plant picker is discarded. The backend returns `responseClass: informational` when the selected plants have no loaded budget (`backend/src/chat/chat.service.ts:639-646`), but `resolveContinueResponse` accepts only success, clarification, and policy-block responses before this branch converts everything else into the plant-choice error. Thus a multi-plant reader who chooses CHIR for an over-budget question keeps the picker and sees “That choice could not be applied” instead of the required informational answer. The new test bypasses this path by submitting the informational fixture as a separate top-level question. Accept the informational continuation and test it through the picker.

findings.body: All new UI proofs inject fabricated `AskResponse` objects through `mocks.ask` in jsdom. The repository has no Playwright test/config or test command driving a browser through the running API with a real database and user, while these user-facing items require that boundary. Consequently the suite cannot prove that real responses produce the plant readout, budget dashes/left-out state, or row-specific transaction click. Add a committed Playwright flow covering these results through the actual Ask entry point.

findings.body: The only new composite-key interaction test covers `gl_code × plant`, and even it clicks/asserts only CHIR's link. The `leaf_key × plant` case in the display-name loop checks only the plant cell; the existing statement drill test is single-dimensional. No test creates DUB and CHIR rows sharing one leaf key and verifies their independent labels, budget states, drill buttons, and CHIR row key, so a statement-specific composite lookup regression would pass. Extend the branch-owned panel test with that named leaf and assert both links in the GL case.
